Most of the efforts in the HOST Surface Protection Subproject were focused on thermal barrier coating (TBC) life prediction in fiscal year 1986.
The TBC life prediction element was divided into contractual, grant, and in-house efforts.
The contracts with Pratt & Whitney, GE, and Garrett were designed to produce 'engine-capable' TBC life-prediction models.
The grant with Cleveland State University focused on finite-element modeling of TBC stress states.
The in-house work focused on developing laboratory burner rig tests to simulate the pressures and heat fluxes of aircraft gas turbine engines.
The airfoil deposition modeling work verified the chemically frozen boundary layer (CFBL) theory and showed encouraging results with the local thermochemical equilibrium (LTCE) theory.
Pratt & Whitney developed a preliminary life model as part of the TBC life prediction modeling work.
Coating mechanical and thermal properties were determined, failure mechanisms were elucidated, and stresses were modeled by finite element analyses.
NDE methods were evaluated, and an engine test was conducted by Garrett as part of the TBC life prediction modeling work.
The rig/engine correlation work aimed to provide a laboratory to verify advances in life prediction at pressure levels encountered in gas turbine engines.
The TBC life prediction modeling strategy involved studying failure mechanisms, mechanical behavior, and model verification to develop a comprehensive, design-capable life prediction model.
The in-house rig/engine correlation work focused on developing a high-pressure burner rig to study failure mechanisms, model verification, and provide data for the life prediction model development.
By the end of FY 1986, a preliminary life model had been developed, and coating properties, failure mechanisms, and stresses had been characterized.
The TBC life prediction modeling work was expected to provide the necessary design capability to allow the use of TBCs in the 'prime-reliant' mode on aircraft gas turbine engine components.
The airfoil deposition modeling work aimed to predict the quantity and location of corrodant deposition on turbine airfoils.
